class.name: TerrainLayer
class.brief_description: A single paintable ground material inside a [Landscape3D].
class.description: [TerrainLayer] describes one ground material a [Landscape3D]'s Paint brush can blend in: an albedo texture and tint, an optional normal map (with a strength control), an optional packed occlusion/roughness/metallic ([member orm_texture]) map with scalar tweaks on top of it, a specular value, an optional heightmap for per-layer Parallax Occlusion Mapping (see [member pom_enabled]), an optional per-layer Triplanar Mapping mode (see [member triplanar_enabled]) for surfaces like cliffs where ordinary top-down UVs would stretch, and how large one texture tile is in world space ([member uv_scale]). This resource is pure configuration; it does not store where it is painted (see [TerrainData]'s per-layer weight maps and [method Landscape3D.paint_layer]). [Landscape3D] combines every layer's textures into shared [Texture2DArray]s and blends any number of layers together smoothly at each point of the terrain, weighted by how much of each layer is painted there. Layer textures are resampled to a common size when built into those arrays, so very high-resolution source textures do not need to match each other exactly.

members.member: Multiplies [member albedo_texture] (or, with none assigned, is the layer's flat color), the same convention as [member BaseMaterial3D.albedo_color].
The base color texture for this layer. Until this is set, the layer renders as a flat color (see [member albedo_color]).

Blends [member orm_texture]'s occlusion (red) channel with "no occlusion" (fully lit): [code]0[/code] ignores the occlusion channel entirely, [code]1[/code] uses it exactly as authored. This fades the effect out at low values rather than multiplying it (which would send low values towards full occlusion - black - instead of none).

An optional grayscale heightmap for this layer, used only when [member pom_enabled] is also [code]true[/code] (and, on top of that, [member Landscape3D.pom_enabled] on the [Landscape3D] this layer is painted on - see its description). Brighter areas sit higher (less depth); if unset, this layer reads as flat even with [member pom_enabled] on.
The high end of [member height_texture]'s value range; see [member height_min].

Remaps [member height_texture]'s sampled value from [code][height_min, height_max][/code] to [code][0, 1][/code] before use, for a source texture that doesn't already use its full range (e.g. one whose useful detail only spans 0.2-0.8).

Scales how much apparent depth [member height_texture] produces under Parallax Occlusion Mapping. Matches [member BaseMaterial3D.heightmap_scale]'s range and usable values (internally scaled down for convenience, so typical values are small double-digit numbers, not fractions).
A display name for this layer, shown in [Landscape3D]'s Paint brush layer list.

How strongly [member normal_texture] perturbs the surface normal; [code]0[/code] ignores it entirely (a flat normal), values above [code]1[/code] exaggerate it. Matches [member BaseMaterial3D.normal_scale] exactly (same range and default), applied the same way (Godot's own [code]NORMAL_MAP_DEPTH[/code]).
An optional tangent-space normal map for this layer. If unset, the layer uses a flat normal (no extra surface detail beyond the terrain's own geometry).

An optional packed occlusion (red channel), roughness (green channel), and metallic (blue channel) texture for this layer, matching the convention used elsewhere in Godot (see [member BaseMaterial3D.orm_texture]). If unset, the layer uses no occlusion, medium roughness, and no metallic before [member ao_strength]/[member roughness] are applied.

If [code]true[/code] (and [member Landscape3D.pom_enabled] is also [code]true[/code] on the terrain this layer is painted on), this layer uses [member height_texture] for Parallax Occlusion Mapping. Per-layer rather than terrain-wide, since a layer with no real height detail shouldn't pay for the ray-marching this adds to every fragment it covers. Mutually exclusive with [member triplanar_enabled] on the same layer (if both are set, this layer is rendered as triplanar, without POM - matching [member BaseMaterial3D]'s own heightmapping/triplanar exclusivity).
Multiplies [member orm_texture]'s roughness (green) channel, the same convention as [member BaseMaterial3D.roughness].

Specular reflectance for this layer at normal incidence, for non-metallic (dielectric) surfaces; unrelated to [member orm_texture], which has no specular channel. Matches [member BaseMaterial3D.metallic_specular] - the default of [code]0.5[/code] is a reasonable value for most materials.

If [code]true[/code], this layer's albedo/normal/ORM textures are projected from the world-space X, Y, and Z planes and blended by surface normal instead of using a single top-down UV, avoiding the stretching that UV would otherwise show on a steep slope (e.g. a cliff face). Mutually exclusive with [member pom_enabled] on the same layer; see there for how the two interact when both are set.

How sharply [member triplanar_enabled] transitions between its three projections; higher values narrow the blend region around each edge. Matches [member BaseMaterial3D.uv1_triplanar_sharpness]'s range and default.

The size, in meters, that one tile of this layer's textures covers on the terrain. Smaller values tile the texture more densely (a smaller, more repeated pattern); larger values stretch it further. Also used as the tile size for [member triplanar_enabled]'s three projections.
